title: Planted-Violation Self-Testing Architecture Boundary Gate

claims.assertion: Static architectural boundary linters must inject synthetic violations into an ephemeral workspace copy before scanning the target repository, ensuring that dead or decaying rules fail CI immediately.

distilled_learning: Static analysis linters and architecture boundary checkers can silently rot over time as codebases evolve and dependencies shift. The planted-violation self-testing pattern requires the verification script to plant deliberate synthetic violations of every architectural boundary rule in a temporary workspace copy before running against production files. If any rule fails to detect its planted violation, CI immediately aborts, ensuring the verification harness remains perpetually infallible.
